cvEn:
Moshe Goldberg, son of Tova and Haim, was born on the 6th of Av 5690 (31 July 1930) in the city of Lodz, Poland, and attended a public elementary school there. He managed to escape and come through the years of terror and destruction safely. In 1945 he immigrated to the Land of Israel and settled in Jerusalem. For a time he was a member of Hanoar Haoved (the Working Youth movement, a Histadrut youth organization).

Moshe began working as a decorator in one of the shops in Jerusalem. At the outbreak of the War of Independence he enlisted, took part in guard duty, and although he received a discharge from service, he often took part in the defense of the city. He fought in the battles at Notre Dame and Katamon, was sent to the Old City, and belonged to the "Yehonatan" platoon. On the 24th of Iyar 5708 (2 June 1948), he fell at Notre Dame when a shell exploded while he was carrying a message from one position to another. He was buried at Sheikh Badr, and on the 28th of Elul 5710 (10 September 1950) he was reinterred in the military cemetery on Mount Herzl in Jerusalem.
